                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>sibly, he begins with this to give the <ns0:hi>Scribes,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Pha<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />risees</ns0:hi> occasion of some Discourse.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="3">3 And behold, certain of the scribes said with<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />in themselves, This man blasphemeth.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> saith, <ns0:hi>There were certain of the Scribes sitting there, and reasoning in their Hearts, why doth this Man thus speak Blasphemies? Who can forgive sins but God only, ch.</ns0:hi> 2.6, 7. <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> saith. <ns0:hi>The Scribes, and the Pharisees began to reason saying. Who is this which speaketh Blasphemies? Who can forgive sins but God alone?</ns0:hi> It should seem they did not speak it out, <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> saith, <ns0:hi>They reasoned in their Hearts. Matthew</ns0:hi> in the next Verse saith, <ns0:hi>Iesus knowing their Thoughts.</ns0:hi> It seemeth that it was then agreed on all hands, that <ns0:hi>Fo<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>giving of sins was the Prerogative</ns0:hi> of <ns0:hi>God alone</ns0:hi>: And that for man to arrogate to himself such a Power as belonged to God alone, was no less than <ns0:hi>Blasphe<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                           <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>,</ns0:hi> as all ascribings of <ns0:hi>Divine Perfections</ns0:hi> to <ns0:hi>Creatures</ns0:hi> must be. It stands the <ns0:hi>Pope,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Priests</ns0:hi> in hand to clear themselves from this Guilt. It was also agreed by the <ns0:hi>Scribes</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Pharisees,</ns0:hi> that Christ spake <ns0:hi>B<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                           <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>s<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />phemy</ns0:hi> in pronouncing to the <ns0:hi>sick</ns0:hi> of the <ns0:hi>Pa<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>sie,</ns0:hi> that <ns0:hi>his <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                           <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap> were forgiven.</ns0:hi> The reason was, because they did not be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lieve him to be the <ns0:hi>Son of God,</ns0:hi> but lookt on him as meer Man.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="4">4 And Jesus knowing their thoughts, said, Wherefore think ye evil in your Hearts?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="5">5 For whether is easier to say, Thy sins be forgiven thee, or to say, Arise and walk?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="6">6 But that ye may know that the Son of man hath power on earth to forgive sins. Then saith he to the sick of the palsie, Arise, take up thy bed, and go unto thine house.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> repeats almost the same words, <ns0:hi>Mar.</ns0:hi> 2.8, 9, 10. So doth <ns0:hi>Luk. ch.</ns0:hi> 5.22, 23, 24. Christ here giveth the <ns0:hi>Scribes,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Pharisees</ns0:hi> a Demonstration of his <ns0:hi>Deity,</ns0:hi> by letting them know, that he knew their Thoughts. Jesus <ns0:hi>knowing their Thoughts said</ns0:hi>: A thing not competible to Angels, much less to one who is meer Man, yet these blind <ns0:hi>Scribes</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Pha<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />risees</ns0:hi> take no notice of it. <ns0:hi>Wherefore think you Evil</ns0:hi> in <ns0:hi>your Hearts, Evil concerning me</ns0:hi>? I did this, saith he, on pur<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pose to let you know, that I, who am indeed <ns0:hi>the Son of Man,</ns0:hi> and whom you mistake in thinking to be no more than <ns0:hi>the Son of Man,</ns0:hi> hath Power, while he is upon the Earth, and so conversing amongst you, <ns0:hi>to forgive sins,</ns0:hi> and you may make sutable Applications to him for that end. It had been as easie for me every whit, to have said to this sick Man, <ns0:hi>Arise,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Walk</ns0:hi>: And that I will demonstrate to you. <ns0:hi>Then saith he to the sick of the Palsie, Arise take up thy Bed, and go to thine House.</ns0:hi> The same Power is required to the one, as to the other, God by your Confession can forgive sins, and God alone can raise Men from the Grave. The end of my mi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />raculous Operations is to Convince you, that I am he who hath a Power to forgive Men their sins. I therefore chose to pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nounce this Mans sins first forgiven, that I might have the advantage to confirm to you by a subsequent Miracle, this great Truth, that I am the <ns0:hi>Son of God,</ns0:hi> tho you think me no more than the <ns0:hi>Son of Man,</ns0:hi> and that I have a power to forgive Sins upon mens Exercise of their Faith and coming unto me. Now therefore believe, not because of my Word only, but because of the Sign I shew you Confirmative of it.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="7">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:232" />7 And he arose, and departed to his house.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="8">8 But when the multitude saw <ns0:hi>it,</ns0:hi> they marvel<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />led, and glorifyed God, which had given such pow<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />er unto men.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> saith <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 12. <ns0:hi>And he immediately arose, and took up his Bed, and went forth before them all, insomuch that they were all amazed, and glorifyed God, saying, We never saw it on this fashion. Luke</ns0:hi> saith <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 5. <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 25, 26. <ns0:hi>And im<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mediately he rise up before them, and took up that whereon he lay, and departed to his own house, glorifying God. And they were all amazed, and they glorifyed God, and were filled with fear, saying, We have seen strange things to Day.</ns0:hi> They all agree in Sense tho not in Words. With Christs Word there went out a power, inabling him to do what he had commanded him. He immediately <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ands upon his Feet, takes up his Bed, or Couch, that whereon he lay (saith <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi>) and went home in t<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>e s<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ght of them all, so as none could doubt concerning the Cure<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> What effect hath this upon the People? They <ns0:hi>marvel<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />led,</ns0:hi> saith <ns0:hi>Matthew</ns0:hi>; they were <ns0:hi>amazed</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>filled with fear,</ns0:hi> saith <ns0:hi>Luke.</ns0:hi> Here is not a Word of their <ns0:hi>believing</ns0:hi> and own<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing Christ as <ns0:hi>the Son of God,</ns0:hi> which was the great thing the M<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>racle was wrought to bring them to, but blindness was hap<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pened to <ns0:hi>Israel,</ns0:hi> seeing they saw, and could not perceive. The Miracle wrought in them an Aw, and Reverence of him as an Extraordinary Person, and put them into a kind of <ns0:hi>Extasy</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Admiration</ns0:hi>: and the Text saith, <ns0:hi>They glorifyed God,</ns0:hi> but not aright; they praised God, not for sending his Son into the World, to save Sinners, but for <ns0:hi>giving such a power unto men,</ns0:hi> they would still own Christ no more than a Man, tho a Man to whom God had given great power. <ns0:hi>No man can say Iesus is the Lord, but by the Holy Ghost,</ns0:hi> 1 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 12.3. truly to be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lieve, own, and receive Christ as our Lord, requireth the Ope<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ration of the Spirit of Grace, working such a Faith, and Per<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />suasion in us.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="9">9 And as Jesus passed from thence, he saw a man named Matthew sitting at the receit of cu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stom, and he saith unto him, Follow me, and he arose, and followed him.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> hath the same Story, <ns0:hi>Mar.</ns0:hi> 2.14. only he calleth him <ns0:hi>Levi,</ns0:hi> and tells us he was the Son of <ns0:hi>Alpheus. Luke</ns0:hi> also mentioneth it, and calls him <ns0:hi>Levi,</ns0:hi> adding that he was a <ns0:hi>Publi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />can,</ns0:hi> and saith, <ns0:hi>That he left all, rose up, and followed him. Luke</ns0:hi> 5.27, 28. This <ns0:hi>Matthew</ns0:hi> might have also the Name of <ns0:hi>Levi,</ns0:hi> all Interpreters agree him the same Man. All three <ns0:hi>Evangelists</ns0:hi> say, that when Christ called him, he was sitting in the <ns0:hi>Custom-House</ns0:hi> at the receit of Custom. This <ns0:hi>Matthew</ns0:hi> was one of the 12 Apostles, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 10.3. and the Pen-man of this Gospel; his Father <ns0:hi>Alpheus</ns0:hi> was honoured to have four of his Sons Apo<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>tles, <ns0:hi>Iames</ns0:hi> the less, and <ns0:hi>Thaddeus</ns0:hi> (called <ns0:hi>L<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>bbeus) Simon</ns0:hi> the <ns0:hi>Canaanite,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Matthew.</ns0:hi> He was a <ns0:hi>Publican,</ns0:hi> an Officer under the <ns0:hi>Romans,</ns0:hi> to gather the Publick Revenue; it was an odious Name amongst the Jews, but <ns0:hi>Matthew</ns0:hi> to magnify the Grace of Christ in calling him, is not ashamed thus to describe himself both here and <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 10.3. <ns0:hi>He saith unto him, follow me, and he arose and followed him.</ns0:hi> His Word carried a secret Power with it, which <ns0:hi>Matthew</ns0:hi> obeyed by leaving his imployment, and going after Christ.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="10">10 And it came to pass as Jesus sate at meat in the house, behold many Publicanes and sinners came, and sate down with him and his disci<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ples.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> saith <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 5.29. <ns0:hi>that Levi made him a great Feast in his own House, and there was a great Company of Publi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />canes, with others that sate down with them. Mark Ch.</ns0:hi> 2. <ns0:hi>v,</ns0:hi> 15. saith, <ns0:hi>they were many: and they followed him. Mat<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />thew</ns0:hi> touched with the Sense of the free, and infinite Love of Christ to him, maketh Christ a Feast: this speaketh him a Man of some E<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>tate, he invites many to dine with him, some of them <ns0:hi>Publicanes,</ns0:hi> some noted Sinners. He designs Good undoubtedly to such as had been his former Companions, that they might also see the Lord, and be brought to follow him. Grace teacheth a Man to study the Conver<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ion of others, and never dwelleth in a narrow Soul, nor studieth its Concealment from others.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="11">11 And when the Pharisees saw it, they said unto his disciples, Why eateth your master with Publicanes and sinners?<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> hath the same <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 2.16. so hath <ns0:hi>Luke Ch.</ns0:hi> 5.30. on<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ly he saith, <ns0:hi>They Murmured.</ns0:hi> The Pharisees having a perfect Malice to Christ, did not only seek all means to carp at him, but to bring him under a Popular <ns0:hi>Odium</ns0:hi>; this seemed a fair opportunity. The <ns0:hi>Publicanes</ns0:hi> being an order of Persons, who both for the<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>r e<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ployment, and perhaps also their ill Mana<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gery of it, were abominated by the Jews, and reckoned a<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mongst the more Notorious Sorts of Sinners. They therefore come to his Disciples clamouring against their Master, That he kept Communion with Publicanes and Sinners,</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="12">12 But when Jesus heard <ns0:hi>that,</ns0:hi> he saith unto them, They that be whole need not a physician, but they that are sick.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="13">13. But go ye and learn what that meaneth, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">M<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>c. 6.6, <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> Chap. 12.7.</ns0:note> I will have mercy, and not sacrifice: For I am not come to call the righteous, but <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">1 Tim <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>.13.</ns0:note> sinners to repen<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tance.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Mark,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> in the places before mentioned have the same Answer, only leaving out these Words, <ns0:hi>Go ye and learn what that meaneth, I will have Mercy and not Sacri<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fice,</ns0:hi> quoted from <ns0:hi>Hosea</ns0:hi> 6.6. Our Saviour's reply to the Pharisees, to him that duly considers it, will appear very smart. 1. <ns0:hi>They</ns0:hi> were a Generation that laid all Religion upon <ns0:hi>Ritu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />als, Sacrifices and Traditions.</ns0:hi> 2. That <ns0:hi>justified</ns0:hi> themselves, <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> 16.15. and thought they needed no <ns0:hi>Repentance.</ns0:hi> Saith our Saviour, I am the Spiritual <ns0:hi>Physician.</ns0:hi> With whom would they have the <ns0:hi>Physician</ns0:hi> to Converse, but with such as are Sick? Those that are whole (as the Pharisees ac<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />count themselves) think they have no need of my coming a<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mongst them. By their Peevishness at the Acts of Mercy, which I do (and those of the highest Mercy too, healing Souls) they shew that they do not understand, what <ns0:hi>Hosea</ns0:hi> (a <ns0:hi>Prophet</ns0:hi> acknowledged by themselves) long since taught them, That the <ns0:hi>Lord</ns0:hi> desired <ns0:hi>Mercy before Sacrifice</ns0:hi> (for that ap<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />peareth to be the Sense of <ns0:hi>not Sacrifice</ns0:hi> in that Text, both by the next Words, <ns0:hi>and the knowledge of God more then burnt Offerings,</ns0:hi> and by the many Precepts by which God declared, that he did desire Sacrifices <ns0:hi>For I came not to call the Righteous</ns0:hi>: that is, those who are swelled in an <ns0:hi>opinion</ns0:hi> of their own <ns0:hi>Righte<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ousness</ns0:hi>: but sensible <ns0:hi>Sinners</ns0:hi> to <ns0:hi>Repentance.</ns0:hi> First to Repentance, then to the receiving Remission of Sins through me, and E<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ternal Life.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="14">14 Then came to him the disciples of John, saying, Why do we, and the Pharisees fast often, and thy disciples fast not?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="15">15 And Jesus said unto them, Can the children of the Bride-chamber mourn, as long as the Bride-groom is with them? But the days will come, when the Bride-groom shall be taken from them, and then they shall fast.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="16">16 No man putteth a piece of <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 span">
                        <ns0:desc>〈…〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> 
                     <ns0:hi>cloth.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> new cloth into an old garment, for that which is put in to fill it up, taketh from the garment, and the rent is made worse.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="17">17 Neither do men put new wine into old bottles, else the bottles break, and the wine runneth out, and the bottles perish, but they put new wine, into new bottles, and both are preserved.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> hath this same History, almost in the same Words, <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> 2.18, 19, 20, 21, 22. only he saith, that some of the Disciples of the <ns0:hi>Pharisees</ns0:hi> came with the Disciples of <ns0:hi>Iohn. Luke</ns0:hi> also hath it varying little, <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> 5.33, 34, 35, 36, 37, 38. only he saith, <ns0:hi>Fast often and make Prayers,</ns0:hi> and, <ns0:hi>The piece that is taken out of the new, agreeth not with the old.</ns0:hi> And he addeth at last <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 39. <ns0:hi>No man also having drank old Wine, desireth new, straightway,</ns0:hi> for he saith, <ns0:hi>The old is better.</ns0:hi> Which I shall consider, it plainly belonging to this History. <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> beginneth his Narration of this History with telling us <ns0:hi>Chap.</ns0:hi> 2.18. <ns0:hi>And the Disciples of Iohn, and of the Phari<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sees used to fast</ns0:hi>; which is implyed, tho not expressed by the two other <ns0:hi>Evangelists</ns0:hi>; for the <ns0:hi>Pharisees,</ns0:hi> it is plain enough from the <ns0:hi>Pharisees</ns0:hi> boast, <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> 18.12, <ns0:hi>that he fasted twice in a Week. Iohn</ns0:hi> also used his Disciples to a severer Discipline then Christ did (of which we shall afterward hear more) It should seem that the <ns0:hi>Pharisees</ns0:hi> had a mind to make a Division betwixt the followers of <ns0:hi>Iohn,</ns0:hi> and the <ns0:hi>followers of Christ,</ns0:hi> and set on <ns0:hi>Iohns</ns0:hi> Disciples to go and ask an account of this. Hypocrites are always hottest for <ns0:hi>Ritual things,</ns0:hi> as things most fit to raise a Division about. There was no Precept of God for any <ns0:hi>Fast,</ns0:hi> but once in a Year, tho indeed God left People a liberty to <ns0:hi>fast</ns0:hi> oftner, as their Circumstances more fitted, and called for the Duty. The <ns0:hi>Pharisees</ns0:hi> had set up themselves a Method, and would fain have imposed it on Christs Disciples; especially con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sidering <ns0:hi>Iohns</ns0:hi> Disciples complyed with the Practice of fre<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />quent fasts, and seemed to suggest as if Christ set up a <ns0:hi>new,</ns0:hi> and more Jovial Religion. (As if <ns0:hi>Religion</ns0:hi> lay only, or Prin<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cipally in <ns0:hi>Rituals,</ns0:hi> as to which God had set no Rule) The <ns0:hi>Pa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pists</ns0:hi> are at this day the <ns0:hi>Pharisees</ns0:hi> true Succe<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ors in these Arts. Christ answereth them in two particulars. 1. <ns0:hi>He tells them that his Disciples were not as yet under such a Dispensation, as called for fasting.</ns0:hi> 2. <ns0:hi>That his Disciples were new Con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />verts, and to be brought on by degrees to the severer practices of External Discipline, and Godliness.</ns0:hi> This is the Sum of <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 15, 16, 17, 18. this he delivers in Metaphorical Expre<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>sions. <ns0:hi>Can the Children of the Bride-Chamber mourn as long as the Bride-groom is with them? But the days will come when the Bride-groom shall be taken from them, then they shall fast.</ns0:hi> Your Master <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> hath compared me to a <ns0:hi>Bride-groom, Iohn</ns0:hi> 3.29. These my Disciples, are the <ns0:hi>Children</ns0:hi> of the <ns0:hi>Bride-Chamber.</ns0:hi> It is as yet a Fe<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>tival time with them. <ns0:hi>Fasting</ns0:hi> is a Duty fitted to a Day of Mourning and Affliction. It is not yet a time of Mourning for my D<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>sciples: yet do not envy them. There will shortly come a time when, as to my bodi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ly presence, I shall be taken from them: then they shall Mourn, and Fast. The 2<ns0:hi>d.</ns0:hi> thing he saith, he Illustrateth by two Simi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />litudes. First (saith he) Amongst Men no discreet Person will put in an Old Garment, a new piece of Cloth, for they will not agree together, the Strength of the new Cloth will bear no Proportion to the Strength of the old, which by wearing is made weak, so as if the Garment comes to a Stress, the Rent will be the greater. So as to Wine, Men do not use to put New Wine into <ns0:hi>Old Bottles,</ns0:hi> that through much use are Weakened for fear of breaking the Bottles, and spilling the Wines, but they use to put new Wine into new Bottles, to Proportion the thing containing to the thing contained. My Disciples are new<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ly converted. Should I impose upon them the severer Exercises of Religion, it might discourage them, and be a Temptation to them to go back. For as <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> addeth, <ns0:hi>No Man having drank Old Wine, desireth New, for he saith the Old is better.</ns0:hi> Custom is a great Tyrant, and men are not on the suddain brought off from their former Practices, but by degrees. This is a Portion of Scripture which much Commendeth Prudence to Ministers, both teaching their People as they are able to bear, and also putting them upon Duties, with respect to their Stature, and Proficiency in the ways of God. Especially in such things as are but our <ns0:hi>free will offerings to God.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="18">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:232" />18 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Luke 8.41.</ns0:note> While he spake these things unto them, behold, there came a certain ruler, and worship<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ped him, saying, My daughter is even now dead, but come, and lay thine hand upon her, and she shall live.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="19">19 And Jesus arose, and followed him, and <ns0:hi>so did</ns0:hi> his disciples.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> hath this History <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 5.22. <ns0:hi>And behold there com<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />eth one of the Rulers of the Synagogue,</ns0:hi> Jairus <ns0:hi>by name, and when he saw him, he fell at his Feet; and besought him greatly, saying, My little Daughter lyeth at the point of Death, I pray thee come, and lay thine hands upon her that she may be healed, and she shall live, v.</ns0:hi> 24. <ns0:hi>And Iesus went with him, and much People followed him, and thronged him. Luke</ns0:hi> hath it, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 8, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 42. <ns0:hi>adding only that she was his only Daughter: Twelve years of Age.</ns0:hi> Two <ns0:hi>Evangelists</ns0:hi> say, she was <ns0:hi>at the point of Death,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>dying, Matthew</ns0:hi> saith, that he said, <ns0:hi>she was dead,</ns0:hi> (that might be according to his Apprehension) she was so near Death, that he concluded, that by that time he was got to Christ, she was dead. Others ob<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />serve out of <ns0:hi>Greek</ns0:hi> Authors that the particle <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> here used, doth not always signify <ns0:hi>a time past,</ns0:hi> but sometimes, <ns0:hi>a time near at hand.</ns0:hi> But the best answer is, That <ns0:hi>Matthew</ns0:hi> relates the Story Compendiously. It appears from <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> 8.49. That theMaid did dye, <ns0:hi>Matthew</ns0:hi> reports that first, which the Messenger brought them the news of afterwards, as we shall see <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 23. of this Chapter. By the <ns0:hi>Ruler</ns0:hi> here both <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> tell us, is to be understood <ns0:hi>Iairus,</ns0:hi> not a <ns0:hi>Civil Magistrate,</ns0:hi> but one who was <ns0:hi>the Ruler of the Synagogue</ns0:hi> in that place, for in their <ns0:hi>Synagogues</ns0:hi> they had an order, there was one Chief who ordered the affairs of it, and they say the Interpretation of the Law belonged to him. [<ns0:hi>And worshipped him</ns0:hi>] with a <ns0:hi>Civil Worship,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>respect, saying, My Daughter is but now dead</ns0:hi> or dying. One would Judge the latter should be the <ns0:hi>Evan<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gelists</ns0:hi> meaning of the Particle, because of what the other <ns0:hi>E<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vangelists</ns0:hi> say, <ns0:hi>come and lay thine hand upon her and she shall live</ns0:hi>
                     <ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> His Faith riseth not up to the <ns0:hi>Centurions</ns0:hi> Faith, who declared his Faith, that if Christ would but speak the word, his Servant should live. <ns0:hi>Iairus</ns0:hi> desires him <ns0:hi>to come and lay his hand upon her. And Iesus arose and followed him, and his Disciples.</ns0:hi> The Jews thrust Christs followers out of their <ns0:hi>Synagogues,</ns0:hi> he is more kind to the <ns0:hi>Ruler</ns0:hi> of their <ns0:hi>Sy<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nagogue,</ns0:hi> he presently goeth, <ns0:hi>and his Disciples followed him.</ns0:hi> They were to be Witnesses of his Miracles. <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> adds, <ns0:hi>much People followed and thronged him,</ns0:hi> which gave occasion to another Miracle, which Christ did in his way to <ns0:hi>Iairus</ns0:hi> his house, the Relation of which <ns0:hi>Matthew</ns0:hi> giveth us before he perfecteth the Hist<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ry of this Miracle.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="20">20 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Luke 8.43.</ns0:note> And behold, a woman which was disea<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sed with an issue of blood twelve years, came behind <ns0:hi>him,</ns0:hi> and touched the hem of his gar<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ment.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="21">21 For she said within her self, If I may but touch his garment, I shall be whole.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> addeth <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 5.26. that <ns0:hi>she had suffered many things of many Physicians, and had spent all that she had, and was nothing bettered, but rather grew worse; when she had heard of Iesus, she came in the press behind, and touched his Gar<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ment, &c. Luke</ns0:hi> saith, <ns0:hi>the Border of his Garment.</ns0:hi> In the Croud there cometh a Woman, that had a bloody Flux twelve years. Inveterate Diseases are hard to be cured, nor had means been neglected, she had tryed many Physicians, and had spent all her Estate upon them. She came behind him, out of <ns0:hi>Modesty,</ns0:hi> and perhaps <ns0:hi>Shame,</ns0:hi> desiring not be taken notice of. That which induced her to come, was the Fame she had heard of <ns0:hi>Iesus,</ns0:hi> and a persuasion wrought in her Heart, (doubtless by the Spirit of God) that if she could but come to touch the <ns0:hi>Hem or Border of his Garment,</ns0:hi> she should be cured. In this she judged rightly, that Christ was <ns0:hi>all Vertue,</ns0:hi> and that his Vir<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tue was not restrained to his <ns0:hi>laying his hand upon her.</ns0:hi> She believed that the Oyl powred on his Head, was like that pow<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />red on the Head of <ns0:hi>Aaron,</ns0:hi> which ran down to the Skirts of his Garment: But if she thought that she could thus steal a Cure<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> and that Christs Cures Flowed not from his <ns0:hi>Grace</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>good Will,</ns0:hi> but a kind of necessity, herein she wonderfully Erred, and Christ afterward let her know it, tho he pardoned her Mi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stake.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="22">22 But Jesus turned him about, and when he saw her, he said, Daughter, be of good comfort, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Luke 7.50. <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 17.19. <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 18.42.</ns0:note> thy faith hath made thee whole. And the wo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />man was made whole from that hour.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Matthew</ns0:hi> relates this Story shortly, as he doth many others, being only intent upon recording the Miracle. We must here supply something out of <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Luke, Mark</ns0:hi> saith, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 5. <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 29. <ns0:hi>And straightway the Fountain of her Blood was dryed up, and she felt in her Body that she was healed of that Plague. And Iesus immediately knowing in himself, that Vertue had gone out of him, turned him about in the Press, and said, who touched my Cloths? And his Disciples said unto him, Thou seest the Multitude thronging thee, and sayest thou who touched me? And he looked round about to see her that had done this thing. But the Woman fearing, and trembling, knowing what was done in her, came and fell down before him, and told him all the truth. And he said unto her, Daughter, thy Faith hath made thee whole, go in Peace, and be whole of thy Plague. Luke</ns0:hi> reports the same Circumstan<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ces with little Variation, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 8.45, 46, 47, 48. Christ was not Ignorant of this Womans coming, and touching his Gar<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ment, he doubtless influenced her to the Motion, his inquiry was therefore only that the Miracle might be taken notice of, he knew that <ns0:hi>Vertue</ns0:hi> was gone out of him, and had healed the Woman, for he had commanded it so to go out, or she had not been healed, but he desired that the People might take no<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tice that she was healed by <ns0:hi>his Grace,</ns0:hi> not by any <ns0:hi>Magical Vertue</ns0:hi> in his Cloths. The Woman is brought openly to come, and confess it, that she had touched his Cloths, and that she was healed. She feared and trembled, lest she should have of<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fended. Christ comforts her, by assuring her the Cure, and telling her; That her <ns0:hi>Faith in him</ns0:hi> as an Instrumental cause had effected it. We have met with Christ often before, as well as in this Text, and shall again often meet with him, ascribing much to the <ns0:hi>Exercise of Faith.</ns0:hi> And the <ns0:hi>Faith</ns0:hi> to which he ascri<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />beth so much, seemeth not to be justifying Faith, or that Exer<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cise of Grace, whereby a Soul in the Sense of its lost Estate, by reason of Sin, accepteth of him, as its Saviour, and relyeth upon his merits alone for Salvation; for we read nothing of the Per<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sons Repentance for Sin, nor reliance upon Christ for the Sal<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vation of their Souls, or any profe<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>sion of any such thing. Is it then so valuable an Act of Faith to believe that Christ is the Son of God? I answer. 1. Tho <ns0:hi>Faith</ns0:hi> in Christ be the only saving Faith, yet a <ns0:hi>Faith in God,</ns0:hi> being persuaded of his pow<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />er and trusting in him, is an Exercise of Grace, which God (as appeareth in Scripture) much rewarded with Blessings of this Life, it giveth God the honour of his Power, <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi> 2. But secondly, The great truth <ns0:hi>That Christ was the Eternal Son of God,</ns0:hi> Was that, which God more especially aimed at to give the Worlds <ns0:hi>Assent</ns0:hi> unto, and <ns0:hi>Persuasion</ns0:hi> of at this time, and indeed Preliminary, and necessary to Peoples receiving of him as their Saviour, for <ns0:hi>Cursed is he that trusteth in Man.</ns0:hi> It was also the great truth which the <ns0:hi>Pharisees</ns0:hi> and the re<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>t of the Jews did oppose. Hence our Saviour takes all occasions both to Confirm and to incourage this Faith, which was but a persuasion, that he was Clothed with a <ns0:hi>Divine Power,</ns0:hi> and did that which no Man could do, and that he had in him <ns0:hi>Di<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vine goodness,</ns0:hi> ready to relieve mans infirmities, according to that Power. 3. It is hardly possible, that any should truly and seriously believe that Christ being apparently Man, and the Son of Man, should also Exercise a power, which none but God could do, and that they should not believe in him as the Saviour of the World, and be quickened to the use of those means, which he should reveal for their Salvation. For these reasons, amongst others, we may conceive that Christ Predicates this Faith so much in those in whom he found it. This M<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ra<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cle being wrought by our Lord in his way to <ns0:hi>Iairus</ns0:hi> his house, after the first notice he had of the Dangerous Sickness of his Daughter, the <ns0:hi>Evangelist</ns0:hi> now goeth on to give us an account of his perfecting that Good Work.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>

                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ours comforting of him, but <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> mentioneth all, <ns0:hi>ch.</ns0:hi> 8 <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 49.50. <ns0:hi>Matthew</ns0:hi> goes on with an Account of what Chri did in the House, seeing the <ns0:hi>Minstrels</ns0:hi> and the Tumult cau<ns0:g ref="char:EOLunhyphen" />sed by the Mourners there.</ns0:note>

Others think that our Saviour speaks <ns0:hi>Ironically,</ns0:hi> knowing that some of them would so diminish the Miracle, to calumniate him or abate his Reputation. But it is a better Answer, to say that he speaks with <ns0:hi>Reference to their Opinion, she is not dead,</ns0:hi> in that Sense you judge her <ns0:hi>dead,</ns0:hi> so as she shall not come to Life before the Resurrection, she is not so dead<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> but she shall come to Life again; as he said to <ns0:hi>Mary</ns0:hi> con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cerning <ns0:hi>Lazarus, Ioh.</ns0:hi> 11.23. Luke</ns0:hi> by this lets us know. That the Soul is not the <ns0:hi>Crasis</ns0:hi>: Or, some accident to the Body, but a <ns0:hi>distinct Subsistence</ns0:hi> of it self. It is enough for u<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> in those Cases, to believe that God is able to do the thing, and that he will do it, if he seeth it be for our good, he only therefore questioneth their Faith as to his <ns0:hi>Power,</ns0:hi> in their former owning him as the <ns0:hi>Messiah,</ns0:hi> the Son of <ns0:hi>David,</ns0:hi> they had declared that they believed his kindness to the Sons of Men. <ns0:hi>They said unto him, yea Lord.</ns0:hi> We believe thou art able; and we believe thee the <ns0:hi>Messiah,</ns0:hi> come to do good, and we have a Trust in thee thou wilt do it, for this cause we are come, we cry unto thee. <ns0:hi>Then touched be their Eyes,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>said, According to your Faith be it unto you.</ns0:hi> See the mighty Power of the Prayer of Faith. <ns0:hi>Their Eyes were opened,</ns0:hi> that is, their visive facul<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>y was restored, or gi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ven to them. And <ns0:hi>Iesus straitly charged them: See that no man know it.</ns0:hi> It was known they were blind, and Men must know that they now saw. But he Chargeth them not to publish it, as done by him. The word used signifieth to Command with Authority, and with a Threatning annexed, we have met with several such Commands to Persons cured, and none of them observed, nor the Persons blamed by Christ, for not observing them. We must say the Parties sin<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ned in publishing the things, unless the Command was with some Limitations not mentioned by the Evangelists. But we are not able, e<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ther<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> to give a just Account, why, or how Christ commanded them: Nor how they published the things, or were excusable in doing of it.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="32">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:233" />32 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">
                     <ns0:hi>See</ns0:hi> Chap 12.22.</ns0:note> As they went out, beho<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                     <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                  </ns0:gap>d they brought to him a dumb man possessed with a devil.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="33">33 And when the devil was cast out, the dumb spake, and the multitudes marvelled, say<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing, It was never so seen in Israel.<ns0:note place="bottom">Some think this the same mentioned, <ns0:hi>Luk.</ns0:hi> 11.14. as shortly as it is here: The word in the <ns0:hi>Greek</ns0:hi> signifies <ns0:hi>Deaf</ns0:hi> as well as <ns0:hi>Dumb,</ns0:hi> for all Persons who are Deaf from their Birth, are also <ns0:hi>Dumb.</ns0:hi> But it is probable this man was only accidentally Dumb, from the Power of the Devil, that had possessed him, and suppressed his Speech. It is observed that Christ cured, 1 Some that came on their own accord to him, as the <ns0:hi>Woman</ns0:hi> with her Bloody <ns0:hi>Flux.</ns0:hi> 2. Others that <ns0:hi>could not come,</ns0:hi> but were brought to him, as the <ns0:hi>Paralytick</ns0:hi> before mentioned in this Chapter, who was willingly brought. 3. Others, who <ns0:hi>neither came, nor were willingly brought,</ns0:hi> but he occasionally met, <ns0:hi>Luk.</ns0:hi> 7.12. <ns0:hi>Ioh.</ns0:hi> 5.5. <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 9.1. <ns0:hi>Others,</ns0:hi> that were <ns0:hi>brought without their Consent,</ns0:hi> as the <ns0:hi>Demoniack</ns0:hi> before mentioned, and this, in this Verse; his Design was, by these Operations to shew himself <ns0:hi>the Son of God,</ns0:hi> and therefore did not always stay for Peoples volun<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tarily offering him occasions, but sometimes took them, when they were not voluntarily offered, to shew the freeness of his Grace.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="34">34 But the Pharisees said, He casteth out the devils through the prince of the devils.<ns0:note place="bottom">This was not the only time they said so. See <ns0:hi>ch.</ns0:hi> 12.24. <ns0:hi>Mar.</ns0:hi> 3.22. <ns0:hi>Luk.</ns0:hi> 11.15. I shall in my Notes on <ns0:hi>ch.</ns0:hi> 12.24. speak more fully to this Text, where we shall also meet with our Saviour's Vindication of himself, from this impu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tation. At present, I shall only observe the miserable Effects of Blindness and Malice. The common People marvelled, and said, <ns0:hi>There was never seen such things in Israel.</ns0:hi> The Jewish <ns0:hi>Doctors</ns0:hi> are mad, and Charge our Saviour to have made a Contract with the Devil, and to have derived this Power from him. But how did this appear to them? No<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />thing appeared as to any thing which our Saviour had done that could Conduct their reason to such a Judgment: No<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />thing but what led their more charitable Neighbours to a quite contrary Judgment. But something they must say to defame our Saviours Reputation amongst the People, having nothing else, but what the People would have judged false, they thus Charge him; nor are the Children of the Devil to learn his Arts, who when they cannot Charge good and Holy Men with Profaneness, Charge them with Hypocrisie, of which it is impossible they should be competent Judges.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="35">35 And Jesus <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">M<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>r. 6.6. Luk 13.22.</ns0:note> went about all the cities and villages, teaching in their synagogues, and preach<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing the gospel of the kingdom, and healing eve<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ry sickness, and every disease amongst the people.<ns0:note place="bottom">We met with these words, <ns0:hi>ch.</ns0:hi> 4.23. only there it was <ns0:hi>all Galilee,</ns0:hi> by which probably this Text ought to be ex<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pounded, see the Notes there.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="36">36 But when he saw the multitudes, he was moved with compassion on them, because they fainted, <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">
                     <ns0:hi>Were tired and <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                           <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap> down.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> and were scattered abroad, as <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Num. 27.17. Zech. 10.2.</ns0:note> sheep having no shepherd.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> hath something of this, <ns0:hi>Chap.</ns0:hi> 6.34. It pitied him, who came down from Heaven to Earth to seek and to save lost Souls, to see what a Company of People followed him, willing to be instructed, because they were <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>, or as some read it, <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>, tyred and wearied with running after him to hear <ns0:hi>the Gospel,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>, <ns0:hi>Scattered a<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />broad as sheep having no Shepherd.</ns0:hi> Had then the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> at this time no Ministry? They had the Temple at <ns0:hi>Ierusalem, Scribes,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Pharisees,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Priests. Synagogues,</ns0:hi> in other places, where the Law was read, and interpreted. Christ ac<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />counts those People to have no Ministers, who have no Good ones: But either, <ns0:hi>Dumb Dogs,</ns0:hi> that cannot Bark, or <ns0:hi>Lazy</ns0:hi> ones that will not. Such was the Generality of the Jewish Ministry at this time. This moved the Bowels of Christ (so the word signifies.) It is a great Misery when the Congre<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gation of the Lord are as <ns0:hi>Sheep which have no Shepherd, Num.</ns0:hi> 27.17. and so they are when they have no true Pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />phets of the Lord to instruct them, 1 <ns0:hi>Kin.</ns0:hi> 22.17.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="37">37. Then saith he unto his disciples <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Luk. 10.2.</ns0:note> The harvest truly <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> plenteous, but the labourers <ns0:hi>are</ns0:hi> few.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="38">38 Pray ye therefore the Lord of the harvest that he will send forth labourers into his harvest.<ns0:note place="bottom">The plain Sense of these two Verses is this, <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> the <ns0:hi>Baptist,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Christ,</ns0:hi> had now been Preaching for some time, God inclined the Hearts of great multitudes, to follow both the one and the other: There was a great People prepared for the Lord, <ns0:hi>Mat.</ns0:hi> 11.12. <ns0:hi>From the days of Iohn the Baptist, the Kingdom of Heaven had suffered Violence, and the Violent took it by Force</ns0:hi>; men were exceeding fond of hearing the Gospel. <ns0:hi>The Fields were white</ns0:hi> to <ns0:hi>the Harvest</ns0:hi> (as our Saviour expresseth it) <ns0:hi>Ioh.</ns0:hi> 4.35. But there were few that would faithfully deliver the mind of God, there were abundance of idle <ns0:hi>Pharisees,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Scribes,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Priests,</ns0:hi> that spent their times in teaching People their <ns0:hi>Rites</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Ceremonies,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Traditions,</ns0:hi> but the Labourers were few; such must be Gods Gift to the People, and they must be thrust out. No Arguments will be sufficient to perswade Men to the weighty work of them Ministry, with an intention to fulfil it, but the Power of God inclining their Hearts to it: You had need therefore <ns0:hi>Pray</ns0:hi> unto God, that he would send, nay that he would <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>, thrust out Labourers into his Harvest. 1. The inclination and Desire of multitudes, to hear Divine Truth, is <ns0:hi>Gods Har<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vest.</ns0:hi> 2. Ministers work is a Labour, <ns0:hi>Gal.</ns0:hi> 4.11. <ns0:hi>Phil.</ns0:hi> 4.3. 1 <ns0:hi>Tim.</ns0:hi> 5.17. if rightly discharged, it must be with <ns0:hi>Labour.</ns0:hi> 3. God is the Lord of the Harvest. Ministers ought to look upon him as so. 4. None ought to thrust themselves into the work of the Ministry, till God thrust them out, <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> 5.4. 5. <ns0:hi>There a<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>ways were but a few Labourers in Gods Harvest.</ns0:hi> Hence <ns0:hi>Chrysostome</ns0:hi> thought that but a few Mi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nisters would be saved. Our Saviour in this Chapter pre<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />faceth his work, of which we shall Discourse in the next Chap<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ter. <ns0:hi>viz.</ns0:hi> His sending forth his twelve Apostles.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
